common.dataCreditPattern: Data: IAEA Live Chart of Nuclides (ENSDF, NUBASE2020, AME2020), retrieved {{date}}

qValues.intro:
A decay can happen only if its Q value is positive. Q comes from the atomic mass excesses Δ:
Qα = Δ(parent) − Δ(daughter) − Δ(4He)
Qβ⁻ = QEC = Δ(parent) − Δ(daughter)
Qβ⁺ = QEC − 2mec2 = QEC − 1.022 MeV
Qp = −Sp and Qn = −Sn
qValues.unseenNote: "Allowed, not observed" means the decay is energetically possible but too slow to see: the α particle must tunnel, a β decay may be forbidden by spin, or a faster mode wins.

census.title: Stable nuclides by parity of Z and N
census.isomerNote: Ta-180m, an excited state that has never been seen to decay, is the one odd–odd isomer found in nature.

energy.title: Energy release
energy.estimatePattern: From the curve: Δ(B/A) ≈ {{gain}} MeV × {{count}} nucleons ≈ {{energy}} MeV

bindingEnergy.noA5A8: No stable nucleus with A = 5 or A = 8

shells.unbound: Below zero: unbound (beyond the drip line)
shells.hint: Look for the sudden drops just after N or Z = 8, 20, 28, 50, 82 and 126.

isobars.yAxis: Mass excess above the lowest isobar (MeV)
isobars.mattauch: Mattauch's rule: two neighbouring isobars are never both stable.
isobars.oddAHint: Odd A: one parabola, so usually one stable isobar.
isobars.evenAHint: Even A: pairing splits the isobars onto two parabolas, so there can be two or three stable isobars, never side by side.

guides.earth: Age of the Earth (4.5 billion years)

halfLives.linearNote: On a linear scale, every half-life shorter than about 100 million years sits on the axis.
halfLives.survivorsPattern: {{count}} radioactive nuclides outlive the Earth's age.
halfLives.noFit: Select an even–even α emitter to see its element's line.
halfLives.comparisonPattern: Q<sub>α</sub> rises by ×{{qRatio}}, from {{qLow}} to {{qHigh}} MeV; t½ falls by {{orders}} orders of magnitude.
halfLives.sargentPattern: Fitted slope {{slope}} (Sargent's rule: about −5) over {{count}} β⁻ emitters. Points far above the line are "forbidden" decays, slowed by a large change in spin.

decayChains.familyPattern: A mod 4 = {{remainder}}: every member has A = {{family}}
decayChains.equilibrium: After many half-lives of the longest-lived daughter, every member decays at the parent's rate: secular equilibrium.
decayChains.chartTitle: The chain on the chart of nuclides: α steps go down-left, β⁻ steps up-left
decayChains.chainTitlePattern: β⁻ chain at A = {{a}}: chain yield {{yield}} %

notes.i131: I-131 (8 d) collects in the thyroid.
notes.xe135: Xe-135 absorbs neutrons strongly: a reactor poison.
notes.br87: Br-87 is a delayed-neutron precursor; delayed neutrons make reactors controllable.
